# Web Audio API coverage on React Native

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-coverage.ts from conformance/rows.ts. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every piece of the standard Web Audio API, with whether a React Native app gets it through rn-web-audio-compat (on top of react-native-audio-api 0.13.6), how, where, and whether Strudel/superdough and Tone.js (15.1.22) use it. Each implemented row has a self-test: the example app runs it on React Native, and the web demo runs the identical test against the browser's own Web Audio API as the reference (one button per row in both; rows marked No have a disabled button).

- **Covered?** Yes / Partial (works with a documented limit) / No.
- **How**: `react-native-audio-api` = provided by that library as is (sometimes with a fix from this library's patch); rn-web-audio-compat = added by this library.
- **Strudel?** Yes = used by normal Strudel patterns; Opt-in = only by a niche feature (audio device selection, visualisations, offline render); No = unused.
- **Tone.js?** Yes = used by Tone.js's core (its context, Transport, Destination, `Param` / `Signal`) or its everyday sources, instruments and filters (`Oscillator`, `Synth` family, `Player`, `Sampler`, `Noise`, `Filter`, `Envelope`, `LFO`); Opt-in = only by the Tone classes named; No = unused. After the colon: which Tone classes use it.
- **Savings left?** Remaining audio-thread CPU savings, and ones already made.

## ConvolverNode

| Name | Covered? | How | Source | Strudel? | Tone.js? | Savings left? | Self-test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ConvolverNode.buffer` | Yes | react-native-audio-api (patched: an unpatched convolver crashed on the audio thread when it processed before `buffer` was set; it now outputs silence, as the spec says, so the buffer can be set after connecting, as Tone.js's Reverb does). Cost grows with the impulse response length: for reverb, prefer `createFdnReverbNode` | [rnaa.patch](native/rnaa-0.13.6/rnaa.patch) | Yes | Opt-in: `Convolver`, `Reverb` (set after connecting) | Done: `createFdnReverbNode` (C++ FDN reverb, cost independent of length; 41% vs 78% audio load for a 0.6 s reverb on a Pixel 10) | Yes |
| `ConvolverNode.normalize` | Yes | react-native-audio-api; its normalization matches the Web Audio spec formula within about 1 dB | — | Yes | Opt-in: `Convolver` | — | Yes |

## Coverage

Counted per row (rows that group several members count once). Partial counts as half.

| Scope | Rows | Yes | Partial | No | Coverage | Present at all |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Whole standard Web Audio API | 140 | 92 | 17 | 31 | **72%** | 78% |
| What Strudel uses in normal patterns | 74 | 63 | 11 | 0 | **93%** | 100% |
| What Strudel uses, including opt-in features | 82 | 69 | 11 | 2 | **91%** | 98% |
| What Tone.js uses in its core and everyday classes | 57 | 48 | 6 | 3 | **89%** | 95% |
| What Tone.js uses, including opt-in classes | 102 | 74 | 13 | 15 | **79%** | 85% |

The biggest gaps (3D spatialization, media streams, latency reporting, output device selection, the deprecated ScriptProcessorNode) are ones Strudel never touches. Strudel-specific pieces (superdough's worklet processors, reverb, delay) are covered by [rn-strudel](https://github.com/wwrinkle/rn-strudel)'s own COVERAGE.md.

Tone.js reaches further than Strudel. Its gaps here: `listener` (`AudioListener`), which Tone's `Listener` reads on every context initialization, so a Tone.js app needs one, even an inert stand-in, before Tone sets up its context; its AudioWorklet classes (`FeedbackCombFilter`, so `Freeverb`, `JCReverb` and `PluckSynth`, and `BitCrusher`), which load their processors from a Blob URL that `addModule()` can't load; and the opt-in `Panner3D`, `UserMedia` and `Recorder`. Tone also starts its own timer clock (a Worker or `setTimeout`), which stops with the screen locked; `createAudioClock()` can tick it instead (`clockSource: 'offline'`).

## Beyond the standard API

- `FeedbackDelayNode`: a delay with feedback that works on react-native-audio-api (a DelayNode graph cycle does not: the library silently drops cycle edges). C++ kernel.
- `createFdnReverbNode()`: algorithmic reverb whose cost does not grow with its length (C++ kernel), level-matched to a browser's normalized ConvolverNode.
- `createAudioClock()`: setInterval/clearInterval driven by the audio thread, which keeps running with the screen locked on Android (plain JS timers stop).
- `startBackgroundPlayback()` / `stopBackgroundPlayback()`: the Android foreground-service notification that keeps audio alive under screen lock.
- `registerKernel()` / `createNativeKernelNode()`: run your own C++ DSP kernel in the graph (see native/README.md).
- `measureAudioLoad()`, `assertNativeKernels()`: audio-thread load and native build checks.
